q: You lift a 10 kg crate 1.0 m upwards and then carry it 5.0 m horizontally at a steady speed. How much work does your supporting force do in total?
a: About 98 J. The lift does the work $W = mgh = 10\,\text{kg} \cdot 9.81\,\text{m/s}^2 \cdot 1.0\,\text{m} \approx 98\,\text{J}$. Carrying it horizontally does no work, because the force is perpendicular to the motion.

q: In an $(s, F)$ graph the force is a horizontal segment at the height 40 N from 0 to 0.50 m. What does the area between the graph and the $s$-axis tell you, and how large is it?
a: The area tells you the work done by the force: $40\,\text{N} \cdot 0.50\,\text{m} = 20\,\text{J}$.

q: Two lifts raise the same load to the same height, one twice as fast. Which one does more work, and which has the greater power?
a: Both do the same work. The faster lift has twice the power.
